notes.summary: Primary-source premises checked for arbitrary compact Hermitian backgrounds; the source dd^c is twice D. Clipped solvability, the nonclosed integration lemma, normalized L1 bounds and volume-capacity estimates apply. Historical capacity results are attributed; they do not resolve original S04.
notes.detailedSummary: Records the indispensable external statements and their hypotheses, and converts the primary operator i partial barpartial/pi by applying it to 2h with unchanged potentials. Distinguishes the supplied threshold and dual facts from historical results. The volume estimate extends from compact to Borel sets by inner regularity. A displayed historical mass-constant discrepancy is diagnostic only; the reconstructed proof does not use it.
notes.text:
These are checked external premises, not newly proved theorems. Throughout, potentials are genuine canonical representatives and products are the ordinary bounded-potential Hermitian products. No closedness or positive bounded-potential mass infimum is required.

The primary source [Kołodziej–Nguyen, Weak solutions to the complex Monge–Ampère equation on Hermitian manifolds](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5491), v2 (2015), supplies Theorem 0.1: every nonzero nonnegative L^p density, p>1, has a continuous solution with a finite positive scalar. Its Lemma 2.1 states, for bounded background-psh a,b,v_i and T=product_i(background+dd^c v_i), with n−1 factors,
∫_{a<b} dd^c b∧T ≤ ∫_{a<b} dd^c a∧T + ∫_{a<b}(b−a)dd^c T.
Proposition 1.2 gives uniform-convergence passage for bounded Hermitian products. The density need not be strictly positive. This source uses dd^c=i∂bar∂/π.

Our convention is D=i∂bar∂/(2π) and d^c=i(bar∂−∂)/(4π), so dd^c=D. Apply the source with background 2h and the SAME potentials. Its forms are 2(h+Du), its capacity is 2^n cap_h, and both sides of its integration lemma scale by 2^n. Its equation with density g dV/h^n divides by 2^n to give (h+Du)^n=cg dV. Thus the scalar is unchanged and capacity competitors retain their original range.

[Dinew–Kołodziej, Pluripotential estimates on compact Hermitian manifolds](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.3937), v1 (2009), Proposition 2.1 gives a uniform L^1 bound for background-psh potentials with supremum zero. Corollary 2.4 gives, for nonnegative F∈L^p, p>1, and compact K,
∫_K Fω^n ≤ C_p‖F‖_p cap_ω(K) exp(−c cap_ω(K)^(−1/n)).
These preliminary results have no mass-invariance hypothesis. Apply them with background 2h and the operator conversion above. Taking F=dV/(2h)^n gives
 dV(K) ≤ C cap_h(K) exp(−c cap_h(K)^(−1/n)).
Inner regularity of dV and monotonicity of t exp(−ct^(−1/n)) extend this to every Borel set. In particular, for small positive capacity, dV(E)≤C exp(−c cap_h(E)^(−1/n)); capacity zero implies volume zero. Numerical constants are not imported unchanged across conventions.

The scalar-limit characterization of b_h, the full Gauduchon dual formula for rho_h, and the root-tail characterization of D_h^0 are GIVEN background in the input. For a bounded density, that characterization identifies its continuous-equation scalar with b_h of the density.

Historical attribution: [Kołodziej–Nguyen, Continuous solutions to Monge–Ampère equations on Hermitian manifolds for measures dominated by capacity](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00526-021-01944-4), Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 2.5, already establish capacity-dominated existence and bounded-range stability. The arguments below reconstruct the required restricted conclusions rather than importing these final assertions. No literature priority is claimed. In the displayed version of record, (2.16) contains t^n hbar_0(t)/(2^n C), whereas displayed (2.17) places hbar_0(t) in the denominator of V_min. That displayed choice does not imply the subsequent factor-four contradiction. The reconstruction uses its own explicit recurrence and does not use that printed constant.

Evidence and reproducibility: primary_fetch_kn2015.json preserves the theorem, integration lemma and product statements; primary_fetch_final_checks.json preserves the volume estimate and displayed constant discrepancy. Additional responses are primary_fetch_01.json, primary_fetch_02.json and primary_fetch_03.json. The last contains mismatched requested reference IDs; its actual source URLs identify Dinew–Kołodziej. Decisive KN checks were repeated with absolute URLs. execution.md records the environment and retrieval limitation. The original input remains in input.json. These are primary-source observations and checked applications, not a new proof of the historical L^p solvability theorem.

notes.summary: A torsion-controlled comparison and capacity recurrence, retaining legal competitor bounds, give positive near-minimum capacity for power-dominated measures. Uniform convergence passes actual nonclosed Hermitian products; normalized potentials are L1 precompact.
notes.detailedSummary: Derives a mixed-integral recurrence retaining Dtheta and dtheta∧d^c theta. For r=n²Bs epsilon^−3≤1/16, the comparison factor is (1−7r)^−n, bounded by 2^n and tending to one with s. Every original capacity competitor is retained. A halving iteration gives the power-capacity lower estimate. Local mixed-mass bounds prove actual uniform product passage and finite bounded-range capacity. These results do not establish positive lower mass for all bounded potentials.
notes.text:
All arguments use D=i∂bar∂/(2π), d^c=i(bar∂−∂)/(4π), genuine bounded potentials, and actual products. The non-elementary comparison input is the integration lemma checked in n1.

Fix a positive smooth Hermitian theta. Choose B≥1 such that −Btheta²≤Dtheta≤Btheta² and −Btheta³≤dtheta∧d^c theta≤Btheta³, in the sense sufficient for wedging with positive products. Smoothness and compactness give such B. Put L=2^n and eta(epsilon)=epsilon³/(128n²B).

First reconstruct comparison with the torsion terms. Let H=theta+Da and G=theta+Db for bounded theta-psh a,b, suppose G≥epsilon theta, 0<epsilon≤1, and on V={a<b} suppose 0<b−a≤s. Define A_j=∫_V H^j∧G^(n−j), j=0,…,n. Applying n1's integration lemma with T=H^j∧G^(n−j−1) gives
 A_j≤A_{j+1}+∫_V(b−a)DT.

Every H and G factor has derivatives dtheta and d^c theta. The derivative DT consists of terms with one Dtheta and one omitted factor, and terms with 2dtheta∧d^c theta and two omitted factors. The sum of absolute coefficients is at most (n−1)+(n−1)(n−2)≤n². Bound theta² and theta³ by epsilon^−2 G² and epsilon^−3 G³. Depending on whether zero, one or two H factors were omitted, this gives
 A_j≤A_{j+1}+r(A_j+A_{j−1}+A_{j−2}),  r=n²Bs epsilon^−3,
with negative-index terms absent. Both torsion contributions are retained.

If r≤1/16, induction gives A_j≤2A_{j+1}. Initially (1−r)A_0≤A_1. Subsequently A_{j−1}≤2A_j and A_{j−2}≤4A_j imply (1−7r)A_j≤A_{j+1}. Keeping this factor proves
 ∫_V G^n≤(1−7r)^−n∫_V H^n≤L∫_V H^n.
For fixed epsilon the factor tends to one as s↓0. The argument applies to bounded canonical products through the checked integration lemma and assumes no globally smooth exact-background regularization.

Now let a,v be continuous theta-psh, −1≤v≤0, and mu=(theta+Da)^n. For 0<epsilon<1 put m=inf_X[a−(1−epsilon)v] and E_s={a<(1−epsilon)v+m+s}. Every E_s, s>0, is nonempty and open, hence has positive capacity: the competitor w=0 contributes theta^n on every nonempty open set.

For ANY genuine theta-psh w with 0≤w≤1, put b=(1−epsilon)v+tw+m+s. If s,t>0 and s+t≤eta(epsilon), then t≤epsilon/2 and
 theta+Db=(1−epsilon)(theta+Dv)+t(theta+Dw)+(epsilon−t)theta.
It is ≥epsilon theta/2 and ≥t(theta+Dw). On V={a<b}, E_s⊂V⊂E_{s+t} and b−a≤s+t. Comparison with epsilon/2 has r≤1/16. Taking the supremum over ALL original capacity competitors yields
 t^n cap_theta(E_s)≤L mu(E_{s+t}).                                      (1)
The convex-combination reserve is explicitly nonnegative; no illegal competitor scaling occurs.

If mu(E)≤A0 cap_theta(E)^(1+alpha), alpha>0, write q(s)=cap_theta(E_s)^(1/n) and M=(LA0)^(1/n). Then t q(s)≤M q(s+t)^(1+alpha) whenever s+t≤eta(epsilon). Let H_alpha=2/(1−2^−alpha). For 0<s0≤eta(epsilon),
 s0≤H_alpha M q(s0)^alpha.                                              (2)
To prove this, start at s_i and propose t_i=2M q(s_i)^alpha. If t_i<s_i, (1) at s_i−t_i gives q(s_i−t_i)≤q(s_i)/2; continue there. If the process stops, s_i≤t_i, and s0 is bounded by the sum of all proposed steps. If it never stops and s0 exceeds that sum, its limiting level is positive with zero capacity, contradicting positivity of E_s. The geometric sum is at most H_alpha M q(s0)^alpha. This proves (2) without potential capacity compactness.

Take v=0, epsilon=1/2 and s*=eta(1/2)/4. Equations (1)–(2) give
 mu({a<inf_X a+2s*})≥(s*)^(n+n/alpha) H_alpha^(−n/alpha)(LA0)^(−1/alpha)/L.  (3)
This lower bound concerns capacity-dominated measures of bounded continuous potentials. It is not a lower bound for all bounded-potential masses.

Actual product passage is reconstructed locally. Choose a constant closed positive beta=D(A|z|²)≥theta on a coordinate ball. For bounded theta-psh u, S_u=beta+Du is a closed positive Bedford–Taylor current, and
 (theta+Du)^n=Σ_{k=0}^n binom(n,k) S_u^k∧(theta−beta)^(n−k).
Local mixed masses of S_u are uniformly bounded on smaller balls when their potentials are uniformly bounded. Indeed, for a cutoff chi and closed positive mixed current R, ∫chi Dv∧R=∫v Dchi∧R. Bound v and Dchi and use nested cutoffs inductively. This proves the needed local Chern–Levine–Nirenberg bound.

If u_j→u uniformly, telescope S_{u_j}^k−S_u^k as D(u_j−u) wedged with the sum of the k closed mixed products. Testing against a smooth form and integrating by parts bounds the difference by C‖u_j−u‖_infinity. Every term in the expansion therefore converges, including its smooth nonclosed coefficient. A finite partition of unity proves actual Hermitian product convergence, including actual total mass. The same local bounds for 0≤w≤1 prove cap_theta(X)<infinity.

For normalized theta-psh functions, n1 supplies the uniform L^1 bound. Their L^1 precompactness follows locally by adding a fixed quadratic to obtain psh v_j. Cutoffs bound the masses of their positive Euclidean Laplacians on smaller balls. Decompose v_j into the Newtonian potential of a cut-off Laplacian measure and a harmonic function. The locally L^1 Newtonian kernel can be approximated in L^1 by smooth kernels, uniformly for bounded-mass measures; harmonic parts have local derivative bounds from their L^1 norms. Both parts are L^1 precompact on smaller balls. A finite cover gives global extraction. Limits take their canonical quasi-psh representatives and retain the current inequality; uniform bounds persist when present.

notes.summary: Target A holds under the additional all-Borel power-capacity bound, with b_h(g)≥C(∫g)^−alpha/(1+alpha) for every nonzero g≤f. The original full rho has quantitative vanishing tails, so f^(1/n) belongs to D_h^0.
notes.detailedSummary: Applies the torsion-controlled recurrence to bounded clips and their exact normalization scalars, combines lower near-minimum capacity with upper mass, and passes to the supplied decreasing scalar limit. Gives an explicit constant depending only on X,h,A,alpha. No selected Gauduchon family replaces the full original supremum. This is restricted to the additional capacity hypothesis.
notes.text:
Target A holds for every smooth positive Hermitian h under the additional power-capacity hypothesis. No positive bounded-potential lower mass is required. The definitions of b_h and rho_h, including the supremum over ALL original normalized smooth D-closed Gauduchon tests, remain unchanged.

Suppose 0≠f≥0 lies in L^1(dV) and ∫_E f dV≤A cap_h(E)^(1+alpha) for every Borel E, where A,alpha>0. Fix nonzero measurable 0≤g≤f and m=∫g dV. Let g_j=min(g,j) and m_j=∫g_j dV. These bounded nonzero densities satisfy the same capacity bound.

By n1 solve MA_h(a_j)=c_j g_j dV with continuous genuine a_j, sup_X a_j=0, and finite positive c_j. The supplied scalar characterization identifies c_j=b_h(g_j). Apply n2 with theta=h, v=0, epsilon=1/2, s*=eta(1/2)/4, L=2^n, H_alpha=2/(1−2^−alpha), and A0=c_j A. Writing Q=cap_h({a_j<inf a_j+s*})^(1/n), equations (1)–(2) give
 s*≤H_alpha(Lc_j A)^(1/n)Q^alpha,
 (s*)^n Q^n≤Lc_j m_j.
Combining and raising to alpha/(alpha+1) yields
 c_j≥C_A m_j^(−alpha/(alpha+1)),
 C_A=(s*)^n/[L H_alpha^(n/(alpha+1)) A^(1/(alpha+1))]>0.
Its dependence is only on X,h,A,alpha, and not on g or j.

By the GIVEN characterization, c_j decreases to b_h(g), while m_j increases to m. Therefore
 b_h(g)≥C_A m^(−alpha/(alpha+1)),
 rho_h(g^(1/n))≤C_A^(−1/n)m^(alpha/[n(alpha+1)]).
Also b_h(g)≤c_1<infinity. This bounds the original rho through its original b_h definition; no test family has been restricted.

For p=f^(1/n), put g_K=f 1_{f>K^n}, with mass m_K→0. If nonzero, the displayed estimate gives
 rho_h(p 1_{|p|>K})≤C_A^(−1/n)m_K^(alpha/[n(alpha+1)]).
If g_K=0 the left side is zero. Its L^n tail norm is m_K^(1/n), so both parts of the D_h norm tend to zero. The supplied tail characterization gives p∈D_h^0.

notes.summary: Target C holds: a common power-capacity bound and two-index directed weighted Cauchy estimates for continuous genuine theta-psh functions in [−1,0] imply uniform Cauchy convergence. Torsion and legal competitor restrictions are retained; no homogeneous uniqueness follows.
notes.detailedSummary: Chooses epsilon as one quarter of the positive supremum difference and a legal torsion-dependent level t. Lower capacity and the weighted difference bound yield a power modulus with exponent [1+3n(1+1/alpha)]^−1. Applying both index orders proves C. The exponent is not claimed optimal.
notes.text:
Fix positive smooth theta. Constants depend on X,theta,n,A0,alpha. Consider continuous genuine theta-psh a,v∈[−1,0], with mu=MA_theta(a) satisfying mu(E)≤A0 cap_theta(E)^(1+alpha). Put I=∫(v−a)_+ dmu and s=sup_X(v−a). If s≤0 there is nothing to prove; otherwise 0<s≤1.

Choose epsilon=s/4 and t=eta(epsilon)/4, with eta from n2. Put m=inf[a−(1−epsilon)v] and E_r={a<(1−epsilon)v+m+r}. Since −s−epsilon≤m≤−s, on E_{2t},
 v−a>epsilon v−m−2t≥s−epsilon−2t≥s/2.
Here eta(epsilon)≤epsilon/2. All recurrence applications are legal: 2t≤eta(epsilon), and t uses at most epsilon/2 of the positive background reserve.

With H_alpha=2/(1−2^−alpha), L=2^n, n2 gives
 cap_theta(E_t)≥[t/(H_alpha(LA0)^(1/n))]^(n/alpha),
 t^n cap_theta(E_t)≤L mu(E_{2t})≤2LI/s.
Consequently
 I≥[s/(2L)]t^(n+n/alpha)H_alpha^(−n/alpha)(LA0)^(−1/alpha).
Since t=s³/(32768n²B),
 sup_X(v−a)≤C I^sigma,  sigma=[1+3n(1+1/alpha)]^−1.
This is a convenient modulus, without an optimality claim. Both Dtheta and dtheta∧d^c theta errors enter through n2.

Apply this with a=u_j,v=u_k, and then interchange the indices. The assumed two-index convergence yields
 ‖u_j−u_k‖_infinity≤C max{∫|u_j−u_k|MA_theta(u_j), ∫|u_j−u_k|MA_theta(u_k)}^sigma→0.
Thus u_j is uniformly Cauchy, proving C. Equality of two Monge–Ampère measures alone does not supply this weighted Cauchy hypothesis, so no homogeneous uniqueness follows.

notes.summary: Target B holds under A in the bounded continuous genuine h-psh class: MA_h(phi)=b_h(f)f dV, supremum zero, with finite strictly positive coefficient and actual mass. Potential compactness and actual product passage are proved without uniform higher Lp bounds on clips.
notes.detailedSummary: The clipped measures are dominated by c_1 f dV and one power-capacity bound. Positive near-minimum mass, normalized L1 bounds and fixed-density absolute continuity force a uniform potential bound. L1 extraction gives weighted Cauchy convergence; scaling permits C and yields a uniformly convergent subsequence. Actual nonclosed Hermitian products pass through the local expansion. This proves existence only under the extra capacity hypothesis, without whole-family potential uniqueness.
notes.text:
Target B holds under A in the specified class PSH(X,h)∩C^0(X), with genuine representatives and supremum zero. For a bounded potential its ordinary Hermitian product equals its extended truncation-defined product. No homogeneous uniqueness is asserted.

Let f_j=min(f,j). By n1 choose continuous genuine phi_j, sup_X phi_j=0, solving MA_h(phi_j)=c_j f_j dV. By supplied background c_j=b_h(f_j) decreases to b=b_h(f). By n3,
 0<C_A(∫f dV)^(−alpha/(alpha+1))≤c_j≤c_1<infinity.
Thus 0<b<infinity. The actual measures mu_j satisfy mu_j≤c_1 f dV and mu_j(E)≤c_1 A cap_h(E)^(1+alpha). No uniform L^p bound for the clips has been used.

We prove uniform potential bounds. Set s*=eta_h(1/2)/4. Equation (3) of n2 supplies v*>0 independent of j such that
 mu_j({phi_j<inf_X phi_j+2s*})≥v*.
The normalized L^1 bound in n1 gives ∫|phi_j|dV≤M1. If H_j=−inf phi_j→infinity along a subsequence, the displayed set has volume at most M1/(H_j−2s*). Absolute continuity of the integral of the FIXED f∈L^1 then gives
 mu_j({phi_j<−H_j+2s*})≤c_1∫_{phi_j<−H_j+2s*}f dV→0,
a contradiction. Therefore −H≤phi_j≤0 for some finite H≥1.

By n2's L^1 compactness, extract a subsequence converging in L^1(dV), hence in smooth-volume measure, to a canonical bounded h-psh limit. The subsequence is Cauchy in that measure. Since |phi_j−phi_k|≤2H,
 ∫|phi_j−phi_k|f dV→0.
Indeed, split at |phi_j−phi_k|≤tau. This part contributes at most tau∫f; the complement contributes at most 2H times the integral of f over a set whose volume tends to zero. First send the indices to infinity, then tau to zero. This is the necessary weighted potential estimate; scalar convergence alone supplies none of it.

Set theta=h/H and u_j=phi_j/H. Then u_j∈PSH(X,theta)∩C^0(X), −1≤u_j≤0, and MA_theta(u_j)=H^−n mu_j. Capacities satisfy
 H^−n cap_h(E)≤cap_theta(E)≤cap_h(E).
For the left inequality, w/H is a legal theta competitor for every h competitor w. For the right, a theta competitor is an h competitor and theta+Dw≤h+Dw. Hence
 MA_theta(u_j)(E)≤c_1 A H^(n alpha)cap_theta(E)^(1+alpha).
Also ∫|u_j−u_k|MA_theta(u_j)≤c_1 H^(−n−1)∫|phi_j−phi_k|f dV→0. Target C, proved in n4, makes this subsequence uniformly Cauchy. Multiplying back by H gives uniform convergence to a continuous genuine h-psh phi with supremum zero.

Apply n2's local closed-beta expansion and telescoping proof. It gives weak convergence to the ACTUAL MA_h(phi), including every lower mixed term involving nonclosed h. Independently,
 ‖c_j f_j−bf‖_L1≤|c_j−b|∫f+b‖f_j−f‖_L1→0.
Therefore MA_h(phi)=b_h(f)f dV exactly. Testing against 1 gives actual mass b_h(f)∫f dV, finite and strictly positive. Since phi is bounded, its extended product agrees with this ordinary product at every sufficiently high truncation level.

This proves existence through a uniformly convergent subsequence. It asserts neither convergence of every choice of clipped potentials, uniqueness, nor an equation for all D_h^0 roots without the added power-capacity hypothesis.

notes.summary: Target D holds on every given h: an explicit continuous non-Hölder radial reference gives actual absolutely continuous f≥c>0 in L1 and in no Lp for p>1, with the all-Borel power-capacity bound, b_h(f)=1 and rho tails O((log K)^−alpha). The exact ball formula concerns the pure top term.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks all radial constants for D=i partial barpartial/(2pi). Smooth radial approximants and mixed flux formulas rule out an origin atom and account for lower Hermitian mixed terms and the cutoff. Rearrangement and the checked volume-capacity estimate prove domination for every Borel set. Restricted existence and sharp small-gap comparison identify the threshold. The actual ball mass also contains positive lower terms. This is a good-tail example, with no constructed zero-lower-mass geometry or unrestricted counterexample.
notes.text:
Target D holds for every GIVEN smooth positive h, whether or not its bounded-potential mass infimum vanishes. The requested exact ball-mass formula is the mass of the PURE INNER TOP term (delta Dq(log|z|²))^n. The actual MA_h(u) has additional positive lower mixed terms on the inner ball; interpreting that formula as its entire actual ball mass would be false.

Fix alpha>0 and p∈X. Rescale a small holomorphic coordinate ball to {|z|<1}. Choose smooth 0≤chi≤1 supported there and equal to one on a smaller ball. Write t=|z|², L_t=1−log t, q(s)=(1−s)^−alpha, q(−infinity)=0, and
 psi=chi q(log t)+1−chi,
extended by one outside. It is continuous, zero at p, smooth elsewhere, and takes values in [0,1]. On the inner ball q′,q″>0, so q(log|z|²) is psh; its origin extension is verified below. On the cutoff annulus Dpsi is smooth and bounded below by −Ch. Thus, for sufficiently small delta>0,
 u=delta psi−delta
is continuous genuine h-psh, sup_X u=0, and h+Du≥h/2.

Let beta=D|z|²=(i/(2π))Σ dz_j∧dbar z_j. For ordinary real Euclidean volume dλ,
 beta^n=(n!/π^n)dλ,  ∫_{|z|<r}beta^n=r^(2n).
For Q(t)=q(log t), the eigenvalues of DQ relative to beta are
 a(t)=alpha t^−1 L_t^(−alpha−1), multiplicity n−1,
 b(t)=alpha(alpha+1)t^−1 L_t^(−alpha−2), multiplicity one.
Therefore the exact punctured pure top density is
 (delta DQ)^n/dλ = delta^n n! alpha^n(alpha+1)/π^n · |z|^(−2n) · (1−log|z|²)^(−n(alpha+1)−1).             (4)

For 0≤k≤n,
 (DQ)^k∧beta^(n−k)=[(n−k)a^k/n + k a^(k−1)b/n]beta^n,
with the evident k=0 interpretation. Its radial shell integral in t is the derivative of t^n[Q′(t)]^k. The exact ball mass, after excluding an atom below, is
 ∫_{|z|<r}(DQ)^k∧beta^(n−k)=r^(2(n−k))alpha^k(1−log r²)^(−k(alpha+1)).    (5)
For k=n and factor delta^n this is precisely delta^n alpha^n(1−log r²)^(−n(alpha+1)).

To verify actual bounded products and absence of an atom, set Q_epsilon(t)=(1−log(t+epsilon))^−alpha. It is smooth and converges uniformly to Q, extended by Q(0)=0. Its tangential eigenvalue is q′(log(t+epsilon))/(t+epsilon); its radial eigenvalue is
 [epsilon q′(log(t+epsilon))+t q″(log(t+epsilon))]/(t+epsilon)²>0.
Thus Q_epsilon is psh. The same cutoff gives smooth psi_epsilon→psi uniformly. Annular derivatives are uniformly bounded, so the same small delta makes h+D(delta psi_epsilon)≥h/2. This verifies the genuine origin representative.

For smooth Q_epsilon, radial integration gives
 ∫_{|z|<r}(DQ_epsilon)^k∧beta^(n−k)=r^(2n)[Q_epsilon′(r²)]^k.
The lower endpoint is zero because Q_epsilon is smooth. For fixed r>0 this tends to (5). Uniform product passage from n2 yields a positive weak limit nu_k=(DQ)^k∧beta^(n−k). Portmanteau on the open ball gives nu_k(B_r)≤liminf nu_{k,epsilon}(B_r), equal to the right side of (5). That expression tends to zero as r↓0 for every k, including n. Hence nu_k({p})=0. Off p these products are smooth and have no sphere mass, so ball-mass convergence gives equality in (5). Integrability of the punctured density alone was not used to infer absence of an atom.

On the inner ball the ACTUAL product is
 MA_h(u)=Σ_{k=0}^n binom(n,k)delta^k(DQ)^k∧h^(n−k).
Every term is positive and is bounded above by a multiple of nu_k since h≤Cbeta. None has an origin atom. Reduce the inner radius so L_t≥alpha+1; then b≤a, and for k<n the densities are bounded by
 C|z|^(−2k)(1−log|z|²)^(−k(alpha+1)).                  (6)
For k≥1 choose 1<p<n/k to obtain higher L^p integrability; k=0 is smooth. Their ball masses are bounded by C r^(2(n−k))(1−log r²)^(−k(alpha+1)). The top term is integrable by (5). The cutoff and exterior products are smooth. Consequently the GLOBAL actual measure is absolutely continuous, MA_h(u)=f dV with f∈L^1(dV), including every lower mixed term and the cutoff.

The strict inequality gives MA_h(u)≥2^−n h^n, hence f≥c>0 almost everywhere. The top term (4) is an inner lower bound for f dV. For any p0>1 its p0-th density power has radial integral comparable, after x=−log r², to
 ∫^infinity exp(n(p0−1)x)(1+x)^(−p0[n(alpha+1)+1])dx,
which diverges. Thus f belongs to no L^p for p>1. Also u(z)−u(p)=delta(1−log|z|²)^−alpha; dividing by |z|^beta tends to infinity for every beta>0. The reference is not Hölder at p.

To prove power-capacity domination for EVERY Borel E, put N=n(alpha+1). On a sufficiently small inner ball the top density F(r)=C r^−2n(1−log r²)^−N−1 is radially decreasing: its logarithmic derivative in t is −n+(N+1)/L_t<0. For a subset of Euclidean volume v, layer cake shows ∫_E F≤∫_{B_r}F for the centered ball of volume v: each superlevel intersection has volume at most the minimum of v and the superlevel ball's volume. Formula (5) bounds this by
 C[1+log(v0/v)]^−N

notes.text:
Restricted targets A, B, C and D are reconstructed in n3, n5, n4 and n6, using the primary premises in n1 and the torsion/product engine in n2. Target E is the necessary scope limitation: these results meet neither original S04 completion criterion.

The original setting remains a connected compact complex X of dimension n≥3, smooth positive Hermitian h, positive probability smooth dV, D=i∂bar∂/(2π), and
 v_minus(h)=inf_{bounded genuine h-psh u}∫_X(h+Du)^n=0.
This is the bounded-potential mass infimum, not a fixed-density Gauduchon volume. The original threshold is the maximal genuine-subsolution coefficient, allowing excess or infinite extended mass, equivalently the supplied clip-scalar limit. Original rho_h retains ALL normalized smooth positive D-closed Gauduchon tests. D_h^0 remains the closure of bounded measurable roots in ‖·‖_Ln+rho_h. No definition is modified.

The first original question asks whether every p∈L^n with finite rho_h has vanishing original root tails when v_minus(h)=0. A negative answer requires an ACTUAL compact Hermitian example proving zero bounded-potential mass infimum, finite rho_h and strictly positive limiting tail norm. Selected tests or an abstract function-space example do not suffice. No such counterexample or universal order-continuity proof is obtained here. The datum in n6 has vanishing tails and cannot give the negative answer.

The second original question asks for MA_h^ext(u)=b_h(f)f dV, with finite prescribed measure, for EVERY nonzero positive-threshold f whose root is in D_h^0, in a specified natural class. Here the equation is proved only under the additional power-capacity hypothesis, in the bounded continuous genuine class. The proof needs common capacity domination of the actual clipped measures to obtain positive near-minimum mass, uniform potential bounds and weighted Cauchy convergence. Original uniform root tails alone have not been shown to imply this hypothesis or an alternative compactness argument. Thus B does not establish the unrestricted second assertion.

The restricted arguments do not require v_minus(h)=0 and remain valid if it holds for the supplied h. No zero-lower-mass geometry is constructed. No lower mass bound for all bounded potentials is assumed or proved: the near-minimum bound belongs only to a uniformly capacity-dominated family. Coefficient identification in the example and subsequence existence in B do not imply homogeneous potential uniqueness.

Historical capacity-dominated existence and bounded-range stability are attributed in n1 to Kołodziej–Nguyen. No novelty or priority certification is claimed. D's radial formula is correct for the pure top term; interpreting it as total actual ball mass would omit positive mixed terms and is rejected. With that precise interpretation, A–D establish a restricted theorem and an explicit non-L^p good-tail density, not a solution of original S04.
